texto: # Output format

encabezado: Output format
texto: When you return the prompt, structure it like this:

encabezado: Output format
texto:
```
Model: <nano-banana-2 | nano-banana-pro | gpt-image-2>
Quality: <low | medium | high>          (only for gpt-image-2)
Size / Ratio: <e.g. 1536×1024 or 16:9>

Prompt:
<the prompt text, ready to copy>

Notes:
- <anything you inferred or assumed because the user did not specify>
```

encabezado: Output format
texto: For edits, also include an explicit preserve-list (mandatory for gpt-image-2, recommended for nano-banana):

encabezado: Output format
texto:
```
Change: <one concrete thing>
Preserve: <face, pose, lighting, framing, geometry, ...>
Constraints: <no extra objects, no drift, ...>
```

encabezado: Output format
Final response style
texto: # Final response style

encabezado: Final response style
texto: Prefer: ready-to-copy prompts, hex colors, concrete materials, named compositions, model-specific syntax (5-slot for GPT Image, natural prose for Nano Banana).

encabezado: Final response style
texto: Avoid: tag soup ("cool, modern, 4k"), vague praise ("stunning, epic, masterpiece" — actively hurts GPT Image 2), negative framing ("no people, no cars" — invert to positive), external comparisons ("like Apple ad" — describe the visual properties instead), numerical lens parameters in Nano Banana prompts (it ignores them).

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: # Image Editing

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: Универсальные паттерны. Логика edit'а различается по моделям:

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: - **Nano Banana:** conversational, без масок. «Keep X same, change Y». Хорошо понимает физику и материалы.

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: - **GPT Image 2:** двухколоночная логика **Change / Preserve / Constraints**. Preserve list повторять каждую итерацию, иначе drift. Опционально `mask_image_url` для точечных edit'ов. Лучшая identity preservation. См. [gpt-image.md](gpt-image.md#editing--двухколоночная-логика).

encabezado: Image Editing
texto: Общее правило: **один edit за итерацию**, не пытайся менять всё разом.

encabezado: Golden Rules
texto: # Golden Rules

encabezado: Golden Rules
texto:
Универсальные принципы. Работают для **обеих** семей моделей (Nano Banana и GPT Image 2).
Для модельной специфики см. [nano-banana.md](nano-banana.md), [gpt-image.md](gpt-image.md).

encabezado: Golden Rules › 1. Start with a Verb
texto: ## 1. Start with a Verb

encabezado: Golden Rules › 1. Start with a Verb
texto: Tell the model the primary operation: "Create", "Generate", "Design", "Transform", "Convert", "Edit". This sets the intent before details.

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: ## 2. Positive Framing

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: Describe what you WANT, not what you don't want. The model understands presence better than absence.

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "empty street" → ❌ "street with no cars"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "clean background" → ❌ "no clutter"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 2. Positive Framing
texto: - ✅ "solo portrait" → ❌ "no other people"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: ## 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: Image 80% correct? Request specific change:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Change lighting to sunset"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Make text neon blue"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 3. Edit, Don't Re-roll
texto: - "Move chart to right third"

encabezado: Golden Rules › 4. Natural Language
texto: ## 4. Natural Language

encabezado: Golden Rules › 4. Natural Language
texto:
❌ Bad: "Cool car, neon, city, night, 8k"
✅ Good: "A cinematic wide shot of a futuristic sports car speeding through a rainy Tokyo street at night. Neon signs reflect off wet pavement and metallic chassis."

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: ## 5. Be Specific

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Element | Vague | Specific |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Material | "shiny" | "brushed steel with matte finish" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Color | "dark green" | "#0d3d2d deep emerald" |

encabezado: Golden Rules › 5. Be Specific
texto: | Position | "on the right" | "right third, bleeding off edge" |

texto: ## 6. Provide Context

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: Context helps model make logical decisions:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for Brazilian gourmet cookbook" → infers professional plating, shallow DOF

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for executive strategy presentation" → infers corporate aesthetic

encabezado: Golden Rules › 6. Provide Context
texto: - "for children's educational app" → infers friendly, colorful style

texto: ## 7. Quote Text Exactly

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: Any text for rendering goes in quotes:

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - Labels: "[Revenue Growth]", "[Net Income]"

texto: - Specify weight: bold, thin, extra bold

encabezado: Golden Rules › 7. Quote Text Exactly
texto: - Specify position: "upper third", "centered"

texto: ## Prompt Template

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors
texto: ## World Knowledge Anchors

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors
texto: GPT Image 2 обладает глубокими знаниями о культуре, эпохах и визуальных стилях. Вместо описания каждой детали — дай модели культурный/временной/жанровый якорь, и она сама заполнит аутентичные детали.

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: ### Три типа якорей

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Era anchors** — временной и географический маркер, который вызывает целый визуальный мир:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Bethel, NY, August 1969" → Woodstock aesthetic без необходимости описывать тай-дай, грязь, сцены

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Berlin, November 1989" → падение стены, толпы, граффити, эйфория

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Tokyo, 1982" → неоновый Shinjuku, аналоговая электроника, ранний cyberpunk

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Cultural anchors** — перенос визуального языка одного культурного объекта на другой контекст:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "{game_title} in {real_city}" → автоматически применяет визуальный стиль игры к реальной локации (GTA style, Persona style, и т.д.)

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Soviet constructivism poster about {modern_topic}" → стиль Родченко/Эль Лисицкого на современную тему

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Ukiyo-e print of {modern_scene}" → японская гравюра с современным содержанием

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: **Genre anchors** — режиссёр/фотограф/движение как линза:

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Peter Lindbergh influence" → сильный Ч/Б, минимальная ретушь, raw editorial

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Wes Anderson palette" → симметричный кадр, пастельная палитра, центрированная композиция

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Studio Ghibli mood" → мягкое акварельное небо, зелёная листва, тёплый ностальгический свет

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Три типа якорей
texto: - "Roger Deakins lighting" → натуральный свет, глубокие тени, кинематографичный объём

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: ### Правила использования

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 1. **Используй как HIGH-LEVEL steering** — якорь задаёт настроение и эстетику, а не заменяет весь промпт

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 2. **Комбинируй с конкретными визуальными деталями** — якорь устанавливает мир, детали устанавливают специфику

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 3. **Не стакай несколько genre anchors** — выбери один. "Peter Lindbergh + Wes Anderson" = каша

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Правила использования
texto: 4. **Era/cultural anchors работают лучше с GPT Image 2** (world knowledge). С Nano Banana результат менее предсказуем — NB больше опирается на явные описания

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto: ### Примеры

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto: **Era anchor + конкретные детали:**

encabezado: Golden Rules › World Knowledge Anchors › Примеры
texto:
```
Create an editorial portrait set in Havana, 1957.

Subject: jazz musician leaning against pastel-colored colonial building,
holding trumpet loosely at his side. Linen suit, open collar.
Lighting: harsh Caribbean afternoon sun, deep shadows under awning.
Format: 3:4
```

texto: # Multi-Panel Compositions

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions
texto: Single-image layouts containing multiple frames, panels, or grid cells. Unlike [storyboards.md](storyboards.md) (sequential images generated one-at-a-time), these patterns produce **one image** with all panels baked in.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions
texto: Core principle: explicitly number and describe every panel. Models need panel-by-panel instructions — vague requests like "show multiple angles" produce inconsistent grids.

texto: ## 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid
texto: **When to use:** Same person shown from 4 angles/crops in one image for an editorial or casting look.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 2x2 grid of four editorial portraits, minimal gap between panels. {background_description}. {lighting_style}.

Subject: {subject_description} — same person in all four panels, consistent identity and wardrobe.

Important Details:
Top-left: front-facing portrait, direct eye contact, shoulders up
Top-right: extreme macro close-up of face — eyes, skin texture, freckles visible
Bottom-left: lower angle looking up, chin slightly raised, confident expression
Bottom-right: side profile, clean silhouette against background

Consistent lighting across all four panels. Skin texture realistic, no airbrushing.

Use Case: editorial photography, model portfolio, casting composite
Constraints: same person in every panel, no wardrobe changes between panels, no extra people, no text overlays
```

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{background_description}` — (e.g., "soft gray studio backdrop")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{lighting_style}` — (e.g., "single key light from upper left, subtle fill from right")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
**Recommended size:** 1024x1024 (square) or 1024x1536 (vertical for portrait emphasis)
**Model:** GPT Image 2 `quality: medium` or Nano Banana Pro (both handle photorealistic portraits well)
**Common pitfalls:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Not specifying "same person" in every panel — model may generate four different people

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Omitting which quadrant gets which angle — model arranges arbitrarily

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 2. 2x2 Editorial Portrait Grid › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - Requesting too-different crops (full body + extreme close-up) creates scale inconsistency within the grid

texto: ## 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage
texto: **When to use:** Hero shot + close-up + action for a campaign visual — horizontal or vertical triptych.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: Three-panel {orientation} collage for {brand_name} campaign. Panels separated by thin white lines.

Subject: {model_description} showcasing {product_description}.

Important Details:
Panel 1 (left/top): Hero wide shot — full figure of model with product, environmental context, lifestyle setting
Panel 2 (center/middle): Close-up product detail — {product_detail_description}, tactile textures, sharp focus
Panel 3 (right/bottom): Action shot — model using/wearing/interacting with product, candid energy, slight motion blur on extremities

Consistent warm golden-hour lighting across all panels. Same model identity throughout.
{typography_instruction}

Use Case: social media campaign visual, brand lookbook
Constraints: same person across all panels, consistent color grading, no stock-photo stiffness, {product_name} must be visible in every panel
```

texto: - `{product_detail_description}` — what the close-up shows

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
**Recommended size:** 1536x1024 (horizontal triptych) or 1024x1536 (vertical triptych)
**Model:** GPT Image 2 `quality: medium` — if text overlay needed, use `quality: high`
**Common pitfalls:**

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 3. 3-Panel Campaign Collage › Template (5-slot format)

texto: ## 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence
texto: **When to use:** Fashion editorial or film-style sequence — multiple camera angles of the same scene in one image.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 6-frame cinematic sequence arranged in a 3x2 grid. Dark film-strip aesthetic with thin black borders. {location_description}.

Subject: {subject_description}, wearing {wardrobe_description}. Same person, same outfit, same location across all 6 frames.

Important Details:
Frame 1 (top-left): Top-down bird's eye view — subject seen from directly above, full body visible against ground/floor
Frame 2 (top-center): Low angle looking up — subject towering over camera, dramatic perspective, sky/ceiling visible
Frame 3 (top-right): Wide isolation shot — subject small in frame, vast environment dominates, sense of scale
Frame 4 (bottom-left): Close-up with slight tilt — face and upper body, Dutch angle, intimate intensity
Frame 5 (bottom-center): Motion frame — subject mid-action ({motion_action}), natural motion blur on limbs
Frame 6 (bottom-right): Grounded final — medium shot, subject at rest, direct gaze, resolving the sequence

Photographer reference: {photographer_style}
Lighting: consistent {lighting_description} across all frames

Use Case: fashion editorial, film lookbook, director's shot list visualization
Constraints: same person and wardrobe in every frame, no costume changes, consistent color grading, no text overlays
```

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)

texto: - `{location_description}` — setting

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{photographer_style}` — (e.g., "Peter Lindbergh desaturated realism", "Helmut Newton dramatic contrast")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto: - `{lighting_description}` — (e.g., "overcast natural light, soft shadows")

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 5. 6-Frame Cinematic Sequence › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
**Recommended size:** 1536x1024 (landscape, 3x2 grid)

texto: ## 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster
texto: **When to use:** Full narrative in one image — 3x4 grid (3 columns, 4 rows) for animation or video pre-production.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto: ### Template (5-slot format)

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › 7. 12-Panel Storyboard Poster › Template (5-slot format)
texto:
```
Scene: 12-panel storyboard poster, 3 columns x 4 rows. Dark background with each panel in a clean rectangular frame. "{title}" in bold white text at the top of the image. Below each panel: scene number and one-line description in small white text.

Subject: {character_description} — maintain consistent character design, proportions, and colors across all 12 panels.

Important Details:
Panel 1: {scene_1} — "{caption_1}"
Panel 2: {scene_2} — "{caption_2}"
Panel 3: {scene_3} — "{caption_3}"
Panel 4: {scene_4} — "{caption_4}"
Panel 5: {scene_5} — "{caption_5}"
Panel 6: {scene_6} — "{caption_6}"
Panel 7: {scene_7} — "{caption_7}"
Panel 8: {scene_8} — "{caption_8}"
Panel 9: {scene_9} — "{caption_9}"
Panel 10: {scene_10} — "{caption_10}"
Panel 11: {scene_11} — "{caption_11}"
Panel 12: {scene_12} — "{caption_12}"

Panels read left-to-right, top-to-bottom (like a comic page). Character appearance, clothing, and color palette must stay identical across all 12 panels — only pose, expression, angle, and environment change.

Style: {art_style}

Use Case: animation pre-production, pitch deck visualization, narrative overview poster
Constraints: all 12 panels must be distinct scenes (no duplicates), character consistency is critical, scene numbers must be legible, {language} captions
Quality: high
```

texto: ## General Multi-Panel Tips

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Panel count vs. detail trade-off:** More panels = less detail per panel. 4 panels allow rich per-panel descriptions; 12 panels need brief, visually distinct descriptions (3-8 words each).

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Subject consistency:** Always include an explicit instruction: "same person / same character / same product across all panels." Repeat key identity markers (hair color, clothing, distinguishing features) rather than saying "same as before."

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Grid specification:** Always state the grid dimensions (e.g., "3x2 grid, 3 columns 2 rows"). Saying "6 panels" without layout instruction lets the model choose an unpredictable arrangement.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Borders and gaps:** Be explicit — "thin white border between panels" or "borderless, no gaps." Default behavior varies by model and is unreliable.

encabezado: Multi-Panel Compositions › General Multi-Panel Tips
texto: **Reading order:** State it: "left-to-right, top-to-bottom" or "numbered 1-9 starting top-left." Without this, narrative flow may be jumbled.

texto: ## Кейфреймы для видео

encabezado: Nano Banana — Specific Rules › Кейфреймы для видео
texto: Nano Banana — image-слой перед motion-слоем. Всё критичное фиксируется на картинке ДО анимации: identity, композиция, aspect ratio, видимый текст, состояние продукта. Видеомодель усиливает любую неоднозначность стилла.

encabezado: Nano Banana — Specific Rules › Кейфреймы для видео
texto: - **Character sheet / hero frame.** Утверди один кадр-эталон персонажа, на него ссылаются все последующие video-промпты.

encabezado: Nano Banana — Specific Rules › Кейфреймы для видео
texto: - **Aspect ratio сразу целевой.** Кампании нужен вертикальный ролик — генери 9:16, а не кропай после анимации (тихая точка отказа).

encabezado: Nano Banana — Specific Rules › Кейфреймы для видео
texto: - **Хэндофф в видеомодель — motion brief, не пересказ.** Движение камеры, движение субъекта, движение фона, длительность, framing lock, запрещённые изменения. Видео-промпт не переописывает то, что уже есть в кадре.

encabezado: Nano Banana — Specific Rules › Кейфреймы для видео
texto: - Downstream любой: Veo 3.1, Kling 3.0, Seedance 2.0/2.5, Gemini Omni Flash (штатная пара Google, 10-сек клипы). Батч картинок → ревью-гейт → в видео уходят только одобренные стиллы.

texto: # Character Design Patterns

encabezado: Character Design Patterns
texto: Reusable prompt templates for character turnarounds, expression sheets, outfit variants, and collectible/card formats. Each pattern uses `{variables}` for customization. Default model: GPT Image 2 (5-slot format) unless noted.

Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto: ## Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto: Use for game or animation pre-production — front, side, and back views of a character on a single white canvas with color callouts and height reference lines.

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto: <!-- Source concept: character model sheet / turnaround sheet for 3D modelers and animators -->

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto:
```
Scene: clean white background, flat even lighting with no cast shadows, thin horizontal height reference lines in #CCCCCC spanning the full width at head, shoulder, waist, knee, and foot level
Subject: {character_name} — {character_description} — shown in three views arranged left to right: front view (facing camera), three-quarter side view (turned 75 degrees right), back view (facing away)
Important Details: all three views share identical proportions and vertical alignment along the height lines, feet on the same baseline, arms relaxed at sides for clear silhouette reading, color callout annotations — small circles of each key color ({color_1} {hex_1}, {color_2} {hex_2}, {color_3} {hex_3}) connected by thin #999999 leader lines to the corresponding material on the front view, fine line weight for height markers, clothing folds and seam lines consistent across all three angles
Use Case: game character pre-production, animation model sheet, 3D reference handoff
Constraints: no background elements, no props in hands, no dramatic poses — neutral standing pose only, all three views must depict the exact same character with identical outfit and proportions, no drop shadows, no gradient backgrounds
```

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto: **Key levers:** `{character_name}`, `{character_description}` (age, build, hairstyle, outfit — be specific), `{color_1}`/`{hex_1}` through `{color_3}`/`{hex_3}` (key palette colors for callouts, e.g. jacket navy #1B2A4A, skin warm beige #D4A574, hair auburn #8B3A2F)

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)
texto: **Recommended model:** GPT Image 2 (`quality: high`) — height reference lines and color callout text require precise rendering

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Character Turnaround Sheet (3-View)

texto: ## Expression Sheet

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Expression Sheet
texto: Use to produce a grid of 6–9 facial expressions for the same character — consistent head angle and art style, with emotion labels under each face.

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Expression Sheet
texto: <!-- Source concept: character expression/emotion reference sheet for animation or visual novel production -->

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Expression Sheet
texto:
```
Scene: white background, 3x3 grid (or 3x2 for 6 expressions) with thin #DDDDDD divider lines, each cell contains one head-and-shoulders portrait
Subject: {character_name} — {character_description} — same head angle (three-quarter left), same hairstyle, same lighting across all cells
Important Details:
  Cell 1: neutral — relaxed brow, closed mouth, calm eyes. Label: "NEUTRAL"
  Cell 2: happy — genuine smile reaching the eyes, raised cheeks. Label: "HAPPY"
  Cell 3: angry — furrowed brow, clenched jaw, narrowed eyes. Label: "ANGRY"
  Cell 4: sad — downturned mouth, glistening eyes, slightly lowered head. Label: "SAD"
  Cell 5: surprised — wide eyes, raised eyebrows, open mouth. Label: "SURPRISED"
  Cell 6: disgusted — wrinkled nose, upper lip raised, squinted eyes. Label: "DISGUSTED"
  {extra_expressions}
  Labels in small {label_font} beneath each cell, #555555 text
  Consistent {art_style} rendering across all cells — skin tone, line weight, shading approach identical
Use Case: animation expression reference, visual novel sprite guide, game character documentation
Constraints: same character identity in every cell — no variation in hair, accessories, skin tone, or clothing between expressions, head angle stays fixed, no hand gestures, labels must be legible
```

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Expression Sheet
texto: **Key levers:** `{character_name}`, `{character_description}` (face shape, skin tone, hair, distinguishing marks), `{art_style}` (clean cel-shaded anime, painterly semi-realism, flat vector illustration), `{label_font}` (condensed sans-serif, monospace, rounded sans), `{extra_expressions}` (add cells 7-9: e.g. "Cell 7: smirk — one corner of mouth raised, knowing look. Label: 'SMIRK'")

encabezado: Character Design Patterns › Expression Sheet
texto: **Recommended model:** GPT Image 2 (`quality: high`) — text labels and consistent facial identity across 9 cells need precise control

texto: ## Anime-Style Character Card

texto: Use for a full character reference card with portrait, full body, key items, and color palette — organized on a white background in a professional concept art layout.

```
Scene: white background, organized reference card layout divided into clear sections with thin #CCCCCC separator lines
Subject: {character_name} — {character_description} — anime-style rendering with clean line art and flat cel shading
Important Details:
  Left section (40% width): full-body standing pose, front-facing, arms slightly away from body to show full outfit, feet visible, confident neutral expression
  Upper-right section: portrait bust — head and shoulders, three-quarter angle, detailed face rendering showing {face_details}
  Mid-right section: {num_items} key items arranged in a row — {item_1}, {item_2}, {item_3} — each drawn at consistent scale with thin outline, labeled in small text below

Use Case: game character documentation, light novel illustration guide, animation production reference
```

texto: ## City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto: Use for urban development campaigns, anniversary materials, cultural exhibitions, or editorial features — a single city view divided down the middle, one half historical and one half modern.

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto: <!-- Source concept: time-split composition — same city view, two eras side by side -->

encabezado: Poster & Illustration Patterns › City Across Two Centuries (Time-Split Composition)
texto:
```
Scene: wide establishing shot of {city_landmark_view}, frame divided vertically down the center — left half shows the scene in {historical_era}, right half shows {modern_era}
Subject: the same geographic viewpoint across two time periods, architecture and infrastructure transforming at the dividing line
Important Details:
  Left half ({historical_era}): {historical_details} — muted {historical_palette} palette, {historical_atmosphere}, period-accurate architecture, {historical_figures} going about daily life, {historical_transport}
  Right half ({modern_era}): {modern_details} — {modern_palette} palette, {modern_atmosphere}, contemporary architecture where old buildings once stood (some landmarks preserved), {modern_figures}, {modern_transport}
  Dividing line: not a hard cut — elements morph and blend across a narrow 5% transition zone (a horse-drawn cart becomes a car, a gas lamp becomes LED, cobblestones become asphalt, a tree grows taller)
  Sky transitions too: {historical_sky} on left to {modern_sky} on right
  Camera angle: elevated three-quarter view (roughly 30 degrees above street level) to show depth of both eras
Use Case: city anniversary campaign, urban development feature, cultural exhibition poster, editorial illustration
Constraints: both halves must depict the SAME geographic location (matching terrain, river, hill positions), transition zone should feel organic not pasted, scale and perspective consistent across both halves, no text unless specified, no anachronistic elements (modern items in historical half or vice versa outside the transition)
```

```
  Brand strip: thin horizontal line or subtle divider in {accent_color} separating the primary content from a bottom section containing "{brand_name}" in small caps and {brand_mark} (logo mark or wordmark)
  Overall palette restricted to {palette} — no colors outside this set
  Text sized for legibility at phone-screen scale — primary text large enough to read in a thumbnail feed scroll
Use Case: Instagram feed post, Facebook post, LinkedIn visual, social media content calendar
Constraints: all text must remain legible at 320px display width, no decorative elements that compete with the message, centered balanced layout, no more than two type sizes (headline + body or headline + brand), background must not reduce text contrast below WCAG AA
```

```
Scene: full-screen desktop UI mockup, {theme_mode} theme, clean {design_system} design system
Subject: {dashboard_title} — analytics dashboard showing {data_domain} metrics
Important Details:
  Sidebar (left, 220px visual width): dark ({sidebar_bg}) vertical navigation with icon + label pairs for {nav_items}, active item highlighted with {accent_color} left border and slightly lighter background, collapsed user avatar and app logo at top
  Top bar: breadcrumb or page title "{page_title}" in medium weight, date range selector showing "{date_range}", notification bell icon with dot indicator

  Chart area (main): {chart_layout}
    Chart 1: {chart_1_type} showing {chart_1_data} — using {chart_1_colors}
    Chart 2: {chart_2_type} showing {chart_2_data} — using {chart_2_colors}
```

texto: ## Personal Color Analysis Board

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: Use to create a visual color analysis graphic from a portrait — seasonal palette classification, clothing color comparisons, and accessory recommendations in an organized layout.

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto: <!-- Source concept: personal color analysis / seasonal color palette board with side-by-side comparisons -->

encabezado: UI Mockups & Social Media Patterns › Personal Color Analysis Board
texto:
```
Scene: white background, organized multi-section layout with thin #E0E0E0 divider lines, clean editorial formatting
Subject: personal color analysis board for {subject_description}
Important Details:
  Section 1 — Portrait & Season (top, full width): {subject_description} portrait photo (head and shoulders, natural lighting, neutral expression) on the left. To the right: season classification "{season_type}" in medium bold text, with a 4x3 grid of small color swatches showing the {num_palette} best colors for this season type ({palette_colors}), each swatch labeled with its name in tiny text below
  Section 2 — Clothing Comparison (middle): two side-by-side panels. Left panel "{good_label}": the subject wearing a top in {flattering_color} — skin looks healthy, face appears lifted and bright. Right panel "{bad_label}": the same subject wearing a top in {unflattering_color} — skin appears washed out or sallow. Small caption under each explaining the effect in 5-8 words
  Section 3 — Recommendations (bottom): horizontal strip with {num_recs} small squares — each showing a recommended item ({rec_items}) in one of the palette colors, with a one-word label below (e.g. "Scarf", "Blazer", "Lipstick", "Frames")
  Visual-first design — images and swatches dominate, text is short labels only
  Clean editorial feel, no decorative flourishes
Use Case: personal styling consultation, color analysis service deliverable, fashion content
Constraints: same person in all panels showing the subject, swatches must be solid flat color (no gradients), labels are short (1-3 words max), no paragraphs of body text, layout must feel organized and scannable, no overlapping sections
```

texto: ### Чеклист микро-деталей

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: Добавляй поверх стандартного verbose — это дополнительные слои, а не замена:

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 1. **Surface wear & aging** — "chipped paint on window frame, hairline scratches on metal surface, green patina on copper fittings, oxidation marks on iron hinges"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 2. **Micro-textures** — "visible pores on skin, individual hair strands catching backlight, fabric weave pattern on linen shirt, grain of weathered wood"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 3. **Atmospheric particles** — "dust motes suspended in light beam, steam wisps rising from coffee cup, pollen floating in golden hour air, fine rain droplets on glass surface"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 4. **Specular behavior** — "specular highlights on metal edges of watch, caustic reflections dancing inside glass bottle, wet surface sheen on cobblestones after rain"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 5. **Fabric & material drape** — "natural fabric folds at elbow crease, gravity pull on loose linen garment, weight distribution visible in heavy wool coat"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 6. **Contact shadows** — "soft contact shadow where cup meets saucer, ambient occlusion in crevices of stone wall, dark line where book spine meets table"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 7. **Environmental reflections** — "building reflections in wet pavement, sky gradient in chrome bumper surface, warm neon glow on skin from nearby sign"

encabezado: Prompt Framework › Cinematic Verbose Mode › Чеклист микро-деталей
texto: 8. **Motion cues** — "slight motion blur on trailing hair strand, frozen splash droplet from espresso pour, wind-displaced fabric edge of scarf"

```
Create a cinematic portrait for coffee brand campaign.

Setting: Small Italian café, early morning. Brass-and-chrome La Marzocca espresso machine in background, oxidation marks on steam wand, hairline scratches on drip tray from years of use. Chipped paint on wooden window frame behind machine.

Subject: Barista in white linen shirt — fabric weave pattern visible, natural folds at rolled-up sleeves, gravity pull on loose collar. Mid-pour with focused expression, visible pores on forehead, individual eyebrow hairs catching backlight.

Atmosphere: Steam wisps rising from espresso cup, dust motes suspended in morning light beam cutting through window. Fine coffee grounds scattered on worn marble counter — soft contact shadow where cup meets saucer. Wet surface sheen on freshly wiped counter edge.

Details: Specular highlights on chrome portafilter handle. Caustic reflections dancing inside glass water carafe on shelf. Warm neon glow of "APERTO" sign reflecting on barista's forearm. Slight motion blur on trailing steam, frozen droplet mid-drip from group head.

Mood: Craftsmanship, ritual, quiet dedication
Lighting: Warm directional light from left window, volumetric through steam
Format: 4:5
```

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: # Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: Use this reference when the user asks to analyze an image and convert it to a generation prompt: **style transfer**, **mood reference**, **"сделай промпт по этой картинке"**, **"перенеси стиль/образ"**, **"проанализируй кадр"**, **"image to prompt"**, **"reverse-engineer this look"**.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: You become a **professional Vision Agent**. Your task is deep cinematic, psychological and optical-colorimetric analysis of the image, translating it into a perfect, highly detailed text prompt for generation.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
texto: The process has two strict steps. Do not skip Step 1. Do not freestyle Step 2.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis
Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: ## STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: Scan the image as **raw data** and extract facts based on:

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Cinematic composition** — Bruce Block's visual structure

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Color theory** — Itten

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Perceptual psychology** — Arnheim

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Directing references** — Spielberg / Scorsese / Tarantino

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: - **Cinematography & colorimetry** — Valentin Zheleznyakov

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION
texto: Evaluate the following four parameter blocks.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: ### 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Who / What:** precise clothing (era, style, materials), age, skin texture, makeup / toning, micro-expressions.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Shot size (after Mascelli):** Extreme Long Shot (ELS), Long Shot, Medium Shot, Two-shot / Three-shot, Close-Up (CU), Choker CU, Extreme CU, Insert shot.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Directing & force placement (Blocking after Kenworthy):** isolating the character at the edge of the frame (anxiety), physical barriers, face turned away from camera, shooting from behind (effect of unknown / powerlessness). Height difference (Level Change) for dominance.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Kinetics & perceptual forces (Arnheim):** visual weight of the object, center of gravity. Internal tension of form (compression / stretching / twisting). Pose, plasticity, motion vectors. Imitation of swift action (motion blur) or monumental stillness.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Color and emotion (Itten):** psychological impact of the local color of the subject.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 1. Subject — psychology and mise-en-scène
texto: - **Gaze:** direction, eyeline anchor, interaction with the frame edges, look into the lens.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: ### 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Setting & Art Direction:** place, era, background, architecture, specifics of materials and surface textures (gloss, matte, rust).

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Three-plane depth (Spielberg):** clear separation into Foreground (with leading details), Midground (action plane), Background.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Figure & ground (Arnheim):** degree of subject isolation, overlapping of forms, mass relationships. Use of reflections (mirrors, windows) to expand context.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Tonal & aerial perspective (Zheleznyakov):** drop in contrast, desaturation, washing out, shift toward cool (blue-cyan) tones in the background.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 2. Environment — geometry and structure of space
texto: - **Frame geometry:** structural framework (axes of symmetry / asymmetry), claustrophobic compression, surface divisions. Illusion of depth via Foreground framing.

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: ### 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast

encabezado: Vision Decomposer — Image-to-Prompt Analysis › STEP 1 — DEEP DECOMPOSITION › 3. Lighting — chiaroscuro, color and contrast
texto: - **Optical & visual contrast (Zheleznyakov):** ratio of lit and shadow areas (OVK). Depth and density of shadows. Exact local color vs. color modified by lighting (valeurs).

texto: GPT Image rewards paragraph-form prompts with explicit spatial reasoning and complex composition descriptions. It interprets relational language ("to the left of", "behind", "in the foreground") more accurately than any other generator. Choose GPT Image when the brief requires precise scene composition, multiple objects, or accurate text rendering.

```
A founder in his mid-thirties with salt-and-pepper hair, wearing a navy crewneck sweater, leans forward at his laptop. texto: - **Don't write Midjourney-style comma stacks**. GPT Image parses them as a list of disconnected concepts
```

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid
texto: - **Don't omit spatial language when the shot has specific composition**, you're paying for the model's strength; use it

encabezado: Adapter: GPT Image (1.5 / 2) › Pitfalls to avoid

name: visual-prompt-forge

description: Generate model-specific prompts from shots.json. Outputs copy-paste-ready prompts for stills (Midjourney, Flux, Ideogram, GPT Image, Nano Banana, Seedream) and motion video (Kling, Veo, Seedance, Hailuo). Also runs a revision mode that reads a critique.json and re-emits prompts for only the failed shots, closing the QA loop. Use when the user asks for image or video prompts, mentions any of those generators, wants AI-generated frames for a storyboard, or hands over shots.json. The prompt half of the pipeline. Composes with storyboard-architect upstream, visual-asset-critic downstream.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers
texto: # Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers
texto: Every image prompt this skill produces is composed from five layers. Four are inputs, one is applied at compose-time. Understanding the layers is the difference between bulletproof prompts and lottery tickets.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: ## Layer 1. Brand Lock

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: **What:** the locked brand parameters for the entire project.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: **Source:** `brand-lock.snapshot.md` referenced in `shots.json`.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: **Constant across:** every storyboard, every shot.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Palette (hex values)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Typography (font names, weights)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Mood descriptors (3–5 adjectives that describe the brand's emotional posture)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - "Never" list (things this brand never does, e.g. "no stock photo aesthetic", "no AI uncanny", "no over-saturated", "no shouting copy")

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Aspect ratios used

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: - Color grade direction

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 1. Brand Lock
texto: This layer answers: **what does the brand always look and feel like?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: ## Layer 2. Series Lock

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: **What:** the locked anchors for this specific storyboard.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: **Source:** `shots.json` → `series_lock`.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: **Constant across:** every shot in this one storyboard.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Character anchor (who's in frame, described identically every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Environment description (where the action takes place, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Lighting setup (direction, source, color temperature, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: - Color grade (filmic look, identical every shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: This layer answers: **what stays the same across this storyboard?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 2. Series Lock
texto: The series_lock is what makes shot 1 and shot 7 feel like the same piece. Without it, every generated frame looks like a different production.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: ## Layer 3. Shot Spec

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: **What:** the per-shot variables.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: **Source:** `shots.json` → `shots[i]`.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: **Variable across:** every shot.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: Contains:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Framing (ECU, CU, MS, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Angle (eye-level, high, low, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Motion (static, push, pull, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Subject (what's happening in this specific shot)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Depth of field

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: - Rationale (audit trail, why this shot, this beat, this moment)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 3. Shot Spec
texto: This layer answers: **what's different about this specific shot?**

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: ## Layer 4. Text Layer

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: **What:** on-screen text composited after generation.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: **Source:** `text-overlays.json`.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: **Never appears in image prompts** (except Ideogram Mode 2 with explicit override).

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: Why text is a separate layer:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 1. **Editability.** Composited text can be revised without re-generating images.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 2. **Quality.** Even Ideogram and GPT Image (the best at text) produce typography that lags professional design tools.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 3. **Animation.** Animated text needs After Effects / Remotion / CapCut. Static rendered text is dead-on-arrival for motion content.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 4. Text Layer
texto: 4. **Brand control.** Composited text uses exact brand fonts and exact brand colors. Generated text approximates.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: ## Layer 5. Generator Adapter

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: **What:** model-specific syntax wrapper.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: **Source:** the relevant `adapters/{generator}.md` file.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: **Variable across:** every target generator.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: This is the only layer the skill *applies* (vs. reads). Layers 1–4 are inputs; Layer 5 is the renderer that turns inputs into a generator-specific string.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: The adapter handles:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Word order (Midjourney leads with subject; motion adapters like Kling lead with camera motion)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Length conventions (Seedream short, GPT Image long)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Parameter syntax (`--ar 9:16` vs `aspect_ratio: "9:16"`)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Layer 5. Generator Adapter
texto: - Idiosyncratic strengths (Ideogram for text, Flux for photoreal, etc.)

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: ## How layers compose

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: For a single shot's prompt:

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: Layer 1 (brand) ───┐

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: Layer 2 (series) ──┼──> Layer 5 (adapter) ──> {generator-specific prompt}

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: Layer 3 (shot) ────┘

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: Layer 4 (text) ────> separate compositing pipeline

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › How layers compose
texto: The adapter pulls from Layers 1–3 and produces a string. Layer 4 lives parallel and never enters the prompt.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: ## Why this matters operationally

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the brand color** → edit brand-lock.md. Every prompt across every storyboard updates. No find-and-replace across files.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the character** → edit series_lock in shots.json. Every shot in this storyboard updates. Other storyboards untouched.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change one shot** → edit just that shot's spec. Other shots unaffected.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Change the generator** → swap adapters. Same shot data, different output file. Zero edits to brand-lock or series_lock.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: **Audit a render** → check brand-lock.snapshot.md to see what version the storyboard was built against.

encabezado: Prompt Anatomy: The Five Layers › Why this matters operationally
texto: This is why guardrails-in-code beat guardrails-in-vibes. Each layer has one job. Changes are surgical. Outputs are reproducible.

texto: # Failure Modes

encabezado: Failure Modes
texto: What goes wrong when generated images don't match the storyboard, and what to fix at the prompt level vs. accept as editorial work.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: ## Failure 1. The "AI look"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Symptoms:** plastic skin, oversaturated colors, eyes too symmetrical, hands wrong, generic stock-photo composition, lighting that's too even, "rendered" feel.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Generic mood adjectives ("beautiful", "stunning", "amazing")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Stable Diffusion crutches ("4k", "highly detailed", "masterpiece") in non-SD generators

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Missing photographic specifics

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - No "never" list applied from brand-lock

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add specific lens and aperture ("50mm prime, f/2.0")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add film stock or camera reference ("Sony FX6", "Kodak Portra 400 film stock")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Add "natural skin texture, no AI rendering artifacts" closing line (Flux, GPT Image)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Verify brand-lock "never" list is being applied, if it includes "no AI uncanny", surface that into the prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: - Use Flux 2 Pro or Midjourney v7 instead of cheaper models for hero shots

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 1. The "AI look"
texto: **Accept editorially when:** the brief is for stylized content where realism isn't the goal.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: ## Failure 2. Character drift across shots

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Symptoms:** same person looks different in shot 1 vs shot 5; clothing changes; hair color shifts; age perceived differently.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Series_lock character string paraphrased rather than verbatim

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - No reference image passed (`--cref`, omni-reference)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Seed not locked

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Too few features described in character anchor (gives generator too much room)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Verify character string is verbatim across every prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Add 1–2 more specific features ("small scar above left eyebrow", "black wireframe glasses")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Use reference image after the first successful shot

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - Lock seed at storyboard level

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: - For Midjourney, use `--cref` with `--cw 50`

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 2. Character drift across shots
texto: **Accept editorially when:** character consistency is genuinely impossible to lock. Budget re-rolls, typically 2–3× per problematic shot.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: ## Failure 3. Text in image looks bad

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Symptoms:** text is misspelled, kerning is off, font is wrong, multiple text elements compete.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Text was put in the image prompt instead of being composited

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Wrong generator chosen (using Midjourney for text-heavy work)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Multiple text elements in one prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - The right answer is almost always: **don't put text in the prompt**. Composite separately from `text-overlays.json`.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - If text must be in-image (poster work), use Ideogram v3 with explicit override flag

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Limit to one text element per prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: - Use simple fonts (sans-serif, clean serif), cursive and decorative fonts fail even on Ideogram

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 3. Text in image looks bad
texto: **Accept editorially when:** the deliverable genuinely requires baked-in text and Ideogram's output is close enough to retouch.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: ## Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Symptoms:** shot 3 has light from window-left, shot 4 has light from window-right, they cut together as a continuity error.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Lighting language paraphrased rather than verbatim from series_lock

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Reverse-angle shots not flagged in rationale

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Generator interpreting lighting ambiguously

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Verify lighting string is verbatim across prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - Be explicit about direction: "from camera-left" not "from one side"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - For reverse-angle shots, flag in rationale and update lighting language for that shot only

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: - For Flux and GPT Image, add the photographic spec ("key light camera-left at 45 degrees")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 4. Lighting direction inconsistency
texto: **Accept editorially when:** lighting drift is subtle enough that color grading will fix it.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: ## Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Symptoms:** the storyboard says text goes in the right third, but the generated image has the subject filling the right third.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Shot subject didn't include negative-space note

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Generator interpreting "centered subject" by default

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Add explicit composition note: "subject framed in left third, right two-thirds open for text overlay"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - For GPT Image (best at spatial reasoning), use percentage references: "subject at left 30% of frame"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: - Re-roll with explicit composition prompt, this often fixes on second try

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 5. Composition doesn't reserve space for text overlay
texto: **Accept editorially when:** image is otherwise great. Reposition text overlay to fit the actual composition.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: ## Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Symptoms:** all locks are in place, prompts look right, but the storyboard feels disjointed when viewed end-to-end.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Color grade language drifting between shots (one says "warm filmic", another says "cinematic")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Aspect ratio drift (some 9:16 generations are taller than others)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Mood adjectives shifting ("calm" in shot 1 vs "energetic" in shot 5 even though brief was uniform)

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Audit every prompt against series_lock and brand-lock, verbatim check

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Verify aspect ratio is identical across all prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: - Lock the brand mood adjectives, same set in every prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 6. Series feels "different" even with locks applied
texto: **Accept editorially when:** the disjoint feel is below the noise floor for the medium (e.g. fast-cut social where each shot is on screen <2s).

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: ## Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Symptoms:** image is technically good but doesn't capture what the brief was actually about.

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Causes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The shot subject in `shots.json` was vague

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The brief context wasn't surfaced into the prompt

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - The generator is producing competent generic output rather than specific intent

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Prompt-level fixes:**

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - Tighten the shot's subject field, what specifically is the audience meant to feel or notice

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - Include a one-phrase intent at the end ("the moment of recognition", "the calm before the decision")

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: - For complex scenes, add a "what this shot conveys" line

encabezado: Failure Modes › Failure 7, "Looks fine but doesn't match the brief"
texto: **Accept editorially when:** generation is close enough that retouching gets there. Don't burn API credits chasing perfect on-prompt.

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: ## When to stop iterating prompts

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: Three signs:

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 1. You've re-rolled the same shot 5+ times with no improvement → the prompt is fine; the model can't render this concept; pick a different shot or different generator

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 2. You're tweaking single words and hoping → you've hit prompt-level diminishing returns; move to image-to-image refinement (Nano Banana) or post-production

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: 3. The image is 80% right and the gap is editorial → ship to post and let the editor finish

encabezado: Failure Modes › When to stop iterating prompts
texto: Generation is one stage in a pipeline. Don't try to make it the whole pipeline.
name: ai-production-director
description: >-

Skill maestra que orquesta el pipeline completo de producción audiovisual con AI — de creative brief a Final AI Video Production Package. Dirige y secuencia las sub-skills instaladas (screenwriter, video, image, ai-video-storyboard, storyboard-architect, visual-prompt-forge, visual-asset-critic, brand-lock-extractor, storyboard-html-preview, visual-media) según el track del proyecto, resuelve conflictos entre ellas y aplica quality gates por etapa. USA ESTE SKILL SIEMPRE que el usuario pida producir un video completo — spot, campaña, reel con narrativa, brand film, explainer o cortometraje — o diga "pipeline completo", "producción completa", "de brief a video", "production package", "arranca la producción", o entregue un creative brief esperando el paquete final. APLICAR TAMBIÉN si pide una parte del flujo pero el contexto revela un proyecto multi-etapa. NO aplicar a piezas sueltas — un solo prompt (usar image/video), un storyboard aislado (usar storyboard-architect), o teoría de cine (usar visual-media).

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: # AI Production Director

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: Eres el director de producción del pipeline. Tu trabajo NO es escribir guiones, prompts ni storyboards tú mismo desde cero — para eso existen las sub-skills, cada una con oficio profundo que tú no debes duplicar ni contradecir. Tu trabajo es:

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: 1. **Clasificar** el proyecto y elegir el track correcto.

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: 2. **Secuenciar** las etapas y cargar la sub-skill correcta en cada una.

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: 3. **Custodiar los gates**: ninguna etapa arranca sin que la anterior pase su quality gate.

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: 4. **Resolver conflictos** entre sub-skills con las reglas de la sección 6 — las decidiste una vez, no se renegocian por proyecto.

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: 5. **Mantener trazabilidad**: todo artefacto downstream traza a un shot ID, todo shot traza a una escena, toda escena al concepto aprobado.

encabezado: AI Production Director
texto: El anti-patrón que este skill existe para matar: "escríbeme un guion y dame prompts" en un solo paso. Eso produce prompts sin dramaturgia, sin consistencia visual y sin trazabilidad. El pipeline produce un paquete de producción.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: ## 2. Selección de track

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: Clasifica el proyecto en el primer mensaje. Si el brief no da los datos, pregunta UNA sola vez, todo junto: plataforma y duración, marca/cliente, objetivo, deadline, y si existen assets de marca.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Criterio | EXPRESS | STANDARD | FILM |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Duración | ≤30s | 30–90s | 90s–10min |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Cliente/marca formal | No | Sí | Sí o pieza de autor |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Narrativa | Un beat (hook→payoff) | Arco simple | Multi-escena, personajes |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Revisiones esperadas | 0–1 | 1–2 rondas | Rondas formales |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Etapas | 4 → 5/6 comprimidas | 0–7 con estrategia ligera | 0–7 completas |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: | Ejemplo | Reel orgánico interno | Spot de campaña, brand film corto | Cortometraje, explainer largo, film de marca |

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: - **EXPRESS**: salta estrategia formal y guion; usa `ai-video-storyboard` para el shot list, luego directo a `image`/`video` para prompts. Sin shots.json ni loop de crítica salvo que el usuario lo pida.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: - **STANDARD**: pipeline completo pero Etapa 1 comprimida (2–3 conceptos en vez de 5, sin documento de territorios) y Etapa 2 comprimida (script directo, sin treatment separado).

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: - **FILM**: todas las etapas, todos los artefactos, todos los gates.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 2. Selección de track
texto: Anuncia el track elegido y el plan de etapas en una línea antes de arrancar. Si el usuario ya trae artefactos de etapas previas (un script, un shots.json), entra al pipeline en la etapa correspondiente — no repitas trabajo hecho.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas
texto: ## 3. Las etapas

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas
texto: Cada etapa declara: sub-skill, entradas, salidas, y gate. El gate se verifica ANTES de avanzar. Si falla, se corrige en la etapa actual — nunca se "arregla después".

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 0 — Brand Lock *(solo si hay marca/cliente)*
texto: ### Etapa 0 — Brand Lock *(solo si hay marca/cliente)*

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 0 — Brand Lock *(solo si hay marca/cliente)*
texto: - **Skill:** `brand-lock-extractor`. Entrada: sitio web, brand book, screenshots o descripción.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 0 — Brand Lock *(solo si hay marca/cliente)*
texto: - **Salida:** `brand-lock.md` (9 secciones, cada valor con fuente y confianza).

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 0 — Brand Lock *(solo si hay marca/cliente)*
texto: - **Gate:** el usuario confirma los valores flagged como estimados. Sin marca formal, usa el Visual Theme de la Etapa 3 como sustituto ligero.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 1 — Creative Strategy
texto: ### Etapa 1 — Creative Strategy

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 1 — Creative Strategy
texto: - **Módulo:** `references/creative-strategy.md` de ESTE skill (no hay sub-skill instalada para esto — el módulo es la autoridad).

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 1 — Creative Strategy
texto: - **Salida:** documento con territorios explorados, 3–5 concept cards, matriz de selección, y dirección narrativa del concepto ganador.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 1 — Creative Strategy
texto: - **Gate:** el usuario selecciona UN concepto. No se escribe una línea de guion con concepto abierto.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 2 — Screenwriting
texto: ### Etapa 2 — Screenwriting

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 2 — Screenwriting
texto: - **Skill:** `screenwriter`. Entrada: concept card ganadora + dirección narrativa.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 2 — Screenwriting
texto: - **Salida:** treatment (solo FILM) → script con escenas XML-tagged, sluglines, acción y diálogo.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 2 — Screenwriting
texto: - **Gate:** cada escena pasa la fórmula de escena de `video`/dramaturgy (deseo + obstáculo + geometría + mirada + ritmo) y la three-jobs rule: cada escena cambia emoción, avanza acción o sube presión. Escena que no hace ninguna de las tres se corta aquí, no en el shot list.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 3 — Cinematic Direction
texto: ### Etapa 3 — Cinematic Direction

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 3 — Cinematic Direction
texto: - **Skill:** `video` (smixs), archivos `dramaturgy.md` y `universal-rules.md` + vocabulario de cámara/luz.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 3 — Cinematic Direction
texto: - **Salida:** documento de dirección por escena: blocking, composición, cámara motivada (cada movimiento responde "¿qué cambió?"), lente, luz, evolución de color, lenguaje de edición, y los 5 anclas de la pieza (una emoción, un motivo, un objeto, un quiebre, una imagen final).

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 3 — Cinematic Direction
texto: - **Gate:** cero palabras del vocabulario prohibido (sección 6.1). Cada decisión de cámara tiene razón dramática escrita.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 4 — Shot Planning
texto: ### Etapa 4 — Shot Planning

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 4 — Shot Planning
texto: - **Skill:** `storyboard-architect` (STANDARD/FILM) o `ai-video-storyboard` (EXPRESS).

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 4 — Shot Planning
texto: - **Entrada:** script + documento de dirección. **Salida:** `storyboard.md`, `shots.json`, `text-overlays.json`, `run.json`, `brand-lock.snapshot.md`.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 4 — Shot Planning
texto: - **Gate:** `tools/validate_shots.py` limpio + six-point dramaturgy check + auditoría de 3 detalles por shot (presión ambiental, micro-acción física, ancla de sonido/motivo). Un shot con cero detalles es filler y se elimina.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 4 — Shot Planning
texto: - Desde aquí, **shots.json es la fuente de verdad**. Ningún prompt, imagen o revisión existe sin shot ID.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 5 — Anchor Images
texto: - **Skills:** `visual-prompt-forge` genera los borradores desde shots.json (adaptador correcto por modelo) → `image` (smixs) es la autoridad de sintaxis final por modelo → el usuario genera → `visual-asset-critic` evalúa cada render contra su shot.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 5 — Anchor Images
texto: - **Salida:** plan de anchors (character refs, environment refs, keyframes por shot clave), prompts finales, y critiques por ronda.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 5 — Anchor Images
texto: - **Gate:** cada anchor crítico tiene critique ACCEPT, con máximo 2 rondas de revisión vía forge en modo revisión (solo shots reprobados). A la tercera falla, se replantea el shot, no el prompt.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 6 — Video Prompts

texto: - **Skills:** `visual-prompt-forge` estructura el prompt de movimiento desde shots.json + anchor aprobado → `video` (smixs) archivo del modelo destino es la autoridad de sintaxis final: motion brief (no re-describir la escena que el anchor ya fija), cámara, blocking, performance, evolución de luz, física, protocolo de diálogo/audio.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 6 — Video Prompts
texto: - **Salida:** prompts de video finales por shot, con continuity blocks entre clips.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 3. Las etapas › Etapa 6 — Video Prompts
texto: - **Gate obligatorio:** los dos checks de `video` (dramaturgy check de 6 puntos + auditoría de 3 detalles) Y, si `aurora-prompt-linter` está instalada, el linter pasa limpio. Un prompt que falla cualquiera de los dos NO se entrega.

texto: ## 4. Interacción con el usuario entre etapas

encabezado: AI Production Director › 4. Interacción con el usuario entre etapas
texto: - Al cerrar cada gate, entrega el artefacto de la etapa y anuncia la siguiente en una línea. En STANDARD/FILM, los gates 1 (selección de concepto), 2 (script) y 4 (storyboard) requieren OK explícito del usuario; los demás avanzan solos salvo instrucción contraria.

encabezado: AI Production Director › 4. Interacción con el usuario entre etapas
